text.p: Swedish telecommunications group AB LM Ericsson Tuesday rang up a 33 percent jump in pre-tax profits in 1996 with its mobile phone unit showing good growth and an improved performance by its public telecommunications unit.

The pre-tax profit of 10.15 billion crowns ($1.4 billion) was slightly higher than a market forecast of 10.03 billion ($1.35 billion) crowns despite the stronger crown wiping 900 million ($122 million) crowns off the result.
"The result was reasonably encouraging and our initial reaction is positive," said Simon Street, a BZW analyst.
Ericsson said revenue for the year rose 26 percent to 124.3 billion crowns ($16.8 billion) while its order bookings climbed 31 percent to 138.05 billion crowns ($18.7 billion).
Ericsson said its radio communications continued to show strong growth in mobile telephones, its main business area.
It repeated an estimate that the number of mobile phone subscribers rose to 137 million in 1996, a jump of 50 million, and that it expected 590 million subscribers in five years.
In its second largest division, public communications, order bookings rose 56 percent to 33.04 billion crowns ($4.5 billion), largely due to orders from Brazil.
